correctness.rationale: Dekking digit recurrence gives x triples (y_n,1-y_n,y_n) and even-index y triples (y_2n,y_2n,1-y_(2n+1)). The y word has no four alternating or six identical consecutive letters. Any period p not divisible by 3 makes a 5p+1 repeated factor of y constant or of x alternating, contradicting the local obstructions. For p=3q, monotone surjective desubstitution F(j)=2floor(j/3)+1_(j mod3=2) converts the full 5p+1 repeated factor of y to period 2q with sufficient length, a strict period descent; x period divisible by 3 reduces to y. The factor x[18:33]=(101)^5 exists by the recurrence. Independent digit-extraction comparison of 12,000 indices and searches for p=1..44 confirm boundaries, but universal bound is proof-based.
